back: Four polypeptides: two heavy, two light; disulfide bonds; variable and constant regions; hinge.
Its variable regions form a binding site complementary to one antigen.
Each antibody has two binding sites, so it cross-links pathogens.
Coating a pathogen with antibodies so phagocytes bind and engulf it more easily.
Antibodies (antitoxins) bind toxins or viral attachment sites, blocking their action.
A plasma cell fused with a myeloma cell: makes one antibody and divides indefinitely.
Immunise mouse → spleen cells → fuse with myeloma → select → clone and screen → culture.
Test line: immobilised antibodies trap hCG-coloured antibody complexes. Control line: binds mobile antibodies; shows test worked.
